task: Deepen flagship changepoint-detector: a closure in the first week after a step (allocate.py row 2)

doc_friction.issue: 7,400 lines; finding the closure rounds needed grep on headings, and the previous round's 'next' named a case (step 1-7 days before a closure) that the data show is the reverse (the 2011-08-29 holiday precedes the 2011-09-01 rise).
200 replayed series x 4 arms take about 50 minutes on this container's 4 cores; the pre-registered sample of 100 per arm cannot resolve a 4-in-100 effect, which earlier rounds did not size for.

deviations.why: Round 3's T4 failed against a reference (fill1) the diagnosis showed was wrong; ran a second pre-registered round (round 4) on fresh seeds with only that bar changed, and said in the pre-registration that it was written after seeing round 3.
deviations.result: Round 4 failed T2 instead; rec3 not shipped, no round 5. The pooled numbers are reported as descriptive only.

writeups: ventures/changepoint-detector/README.md section 'A closure in the first week after a step'
notes: Two pre-registered rounds of a recent-days closure fill (fillClosed recent: 3) against the shipped fill1. Round 3 (seeds 20261121): T1-T3 pass, T4 fails (903 > 887 alerts; the reference arm mutes step alerts). Round 4 (seeds 20261122, U4 against clean): T1, T3, U4 pass, T2 fails (62 < 60+5). Pooled over 227 steps: clean 133, fill1 124, rec3 139. On real data the lost 2011-09-01 alert follows a closure (2011-08-29), not precedes it, so the next item is a closure before a step. Not shipped; recent stays a module option with 2 tests. Local checks: closed-days.test.mjs 10/10; run_venture_tests.py changepoint-detector: ok, 940 tests, 192 s; site page checks ok.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: design a fill, two pre-registered simulation rounds, diagnosis, real-data rerun and write-up by a statistician

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
